description_full: Legacy Housing Corporation engages in the building, sale, and financing of manufactured homes and tiny houses primarily in the southern United States. The company manufactures and provides for the transport of mobile homes, including 1 to 5 bedrooms with 1 to 3 1/2 bathrooms; and provides wholesale financing to dealers and mobile home parks, as well as retail financing to consumers. It also provides inventory financing for its independent retailers; consumer financing for its products; and financing to manufactured housing community owners that buy or lease its products for use in their rental housing communities. The company is involved in financing and developing new manufactured home communities. It markets its homes under the Legacy brand through a network of independent retailers and company-owned stores; and directly to manufactured home communities. The company was founded in 2005 and is headquartered in Bedford, Texas.

financial_summary: Legacy Housing Corporation is a small-cap consumer cyclical business with a $694M market cap on $165M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -14% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 13% against a 9% cost of capital, a 4-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $28M in free cash flow — roughly 17 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.89× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 1.1%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 64% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 3.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
